Results.ReviewText: My In-laws gave me an early Xmas present, a Weber Master-Touch charcoal potbelly, what a cool Xmas present. Anyway I smoked my first turkey ever on Xmas Eve, it was a success. The last couple of years, I’ve been observing and assisting my FIL when he smokes their Thanksgiving turkey on his Weber, so I had a bit of background and all. He gave me an excellent apple juice brine recipe, I brined the turkey overnight in the garage. The brine process really seems to help the turkey hold moisture. The family seemed to enjoy the hickory-smoked flavor.  Regarding the Master-Touch, this is the top-of-the-line of the Weber Potbellys.   The bells and whistles may seem sometimes trivial, but IMO, they are well worth the few extra dollars spent.   For example, the removable ash-catcher is very convenient, and pretty much mess-free, when dumping ashes.  The lid holder is quite convenient.   Plus, the Master-Touch sits a bit higher than the other two models, so that's nice, especially for taller people.   This model comes provided with removable charcoal baskets and the grilling grate that is hinged at each end, to allow for easy replenishing of charcoal.     Looking forward to further Weber potbelly adventures! I think a smoked ham might be in my future! With Weber, the possibilities are endless!
Results.Title: This one has all the bells and whistles!

Results.ReviewText: For years I had a Weber 18” and I drove it hard into the ground after years of continued use, and no cover.  I was gifted a gas grill and used it for 2 or 3 seasons before it gave up the ghost.  I then purchased a used grill on Craigslist trying to save money, but a neighbor’s tree fell on it during a storm, crushing it, this year.  So I was ready to get a kamado style ceramic grill so I could “start smoking.”  I did a TON of research, multiple spreadsheets with pricing, pros, cons, etc, etc.  But I always had the 22” Weber in the back of mind, as I knew I could slay steaks, burgers and fajitas on it.  And to be honest with myself, that was my “Big Three.”  That’s what I’m typically doing anyway, so I shifted my focus from “set it and forget it” smoking, to straight up grilling, which is my true passion.  The pendulum quickly swung back to the 22” Weber, but I had to decide between the 3 versions; entry level, the next step up with the ash/coal catching system, or the Master Touch.  Again, I made another spreadsheet (don’t ask, I may have a spreadsheet disorder, just ask the wife), and made multiple stops at places that carried it.  I eventually went with the Master Touch and haven’t looked back since.  I’ve used it about once a week since using it, and just last weekend, had another couple over for a spontaneous dinner, and my buddy and I bought 4 fairly nice rib eyes to grill up.  Let me just say we had 4 very happy campers while eating.  It was so good, I think I’ll break it out tonight for some fun times.  All in all, I think I put too much time into my decision.  In the back of my mind, I think I knew it was the best grill to get.  I shouldn’t have spun my wheels taking the time to make the decision.  Like I said above, don’t overthink it, just buy it.  You’ll be stoked!
Results.Title: Don’t overthink it, just buy it.

Results.ReviewText: After using a gas grill for a number of years I decided to go back to charcoal.  I had a original Weber kettle about 25 years ago and loved it so when I moved back to charcoal grilling it was the first one I thought of.  This time I upgraded to the Master-Touch and love it!  I assembled it without a problem and after a quick seasoning began grilling.  The charcoal trays made it very convenient to position the coals for either direct or indirect cooking, or a combination.  The grill is well-built and I anticipate many years of outdoor cooking with it.  I also plan to add accessories designed for the Master-Touch, especially the cast iron insert.  I really enjoy cooking with the Master-Touch Charcoal Grill!
Results.Title: A great grilling experience!

Results.ReviewText: I've had my Weber Kettle for over a month now and I feel like I'm part of a "food community". There are so many people out there with great products, helpful videos, recipes and techniques. It takes longer to prepare my grille, true but it is an immersive, relaxing experience. Starting the charcoal using the Weber chimney is a breeze. It's like starting a fire in a fireplace or a campfire. Using the char baskets allows for an appetizing sear. I don't feel like I was ever able to sear like this using propane. Steaks, hamburgers and especially CHICKEN THIGHS are exquisite. My wife complimented the first burgers I cooked as "the best she ever tasted"!  Using wood chunks to smoke with is as easy as tossing split wood chunks on top of the charcoal. My personal favourite so far had been the slow smoked pork ribs using the "snake technique" and apple wood chunks. The simple design and small number of parts, easily disassembled, makes thorough cleaning intuitive. I may not EVER get another propane barbecue!

I bought this grill to replace my years-old weber - their standard kettle grill.  Love the new (to me) features - the grill surface that allows coal to be added, the unit below for catching the spent charcoal/wood, the thermometer and the ability to slide the top into its holder.  I recently bought a wireless meat thermometer... sorry not Weber's... didn't like what I read in the reviews, and using this grill I made two absolutely perfect steaks - one medium (for my wife), and one medium rare (for me), and they could not have come out more perfect.

On the downside, I found the installation of the legs onto the bottom portion of the kettle to be ridiculously difficult.  The fit was way too tight, and it took me almost 10 mintues to get one of the 3 legs installed, and the clip the locks the leg in place fell into the leg and I just plain gave up on it after pulling it out 2 or 3 times and trying again.  The fit was so tight, as mentioned above, I figure it won't matter if the clip is in place or not.  Weber designers - if you read this, please remedy these assemply problems because they were extremely frustrating.

Results.ReviewText: A couple months ago, my very expensive boutique propane grill broke. In the time before repairs were affected, I purchased this grill. We were amazed at how delicious the food tasted. It is unquestionably more flavorful than propane. Using a charcoal chimney (highly recommended) it lights up quick and easy. The upper and lower air flow vent controls allow for easily controlled cooking temperatures. After cooking, the removeable bottom peice makes for easy disposal of spent charcoal ash. What more could you ask for? SInce the return to service of my propane grill, we find ourselves using our Weber more often than our propane grill.

Like all Weber® kettles, it’s built to last with a porcelain-enameled bowl and lid that retain heat and resist rust, peeling, and scratching, and adjustable lid and bowl dampers to fine-tune the heat for perfect results. When it’s time to clean up, the One-Touch™ cleaning system makes it neat and effortless—just swipe the lever to clear ashes into the enclosed, high-capacity ash catcher. Two wheels make it easy to roll this timeless classic to the center of the action, right where it belongs. Because some grills don’t just cook food, they make memories.· Porcelain-enameled finish is scratch and rust-resistant· Room to cook for 6-8 people· Hinged, plated-steel cooking grate fits circular GBS grillware· Included Char-Rails make it easy to arrange charcoal· Lid thermometer makes it easy to see grill temperature· Adjustable lid and bowl dampers let you control temperature· Tuck-Away Lid Holder provides handy space to hang lid· 2 tool hooks included on bowl handle· One-Touch™ cleaning system sweeps ash into enclosed catcher· Easy to move on two durable, all-weather wheels.· Heat-resistant lid and bowl handles· Bottom, wire storage shelf· Durable fuel grate· 3 aluminum legs are rust-resistant and 2” taller· 10-year limited warranty
